summary: A 1910 wooden fire tower on Snow Mountain, replaced in 1914 by a 24-foot steel tower with cab; the cab has fallen off and the summit sits on Penobscot Nation land behind a gate.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the tower as standing with its cab no longer in place. FranklinSites says the cab has fallen off; the date is not given, but the cab was still there in 1967.

access.note: The summit is on Penobscot Indian Nation land, reached through a gate on the road off Route 27. No source says visitors may climb the tower.

visit.trail_note: Drive the dirt road off Route 27 through the gate, then about 5 miles to the trailhead. The trail gains about 1,880 feet. Climbing the bare structure is not documented as permitted.

events.note: Wooden fire tower established on Snow Mountain, per the Maine Historical Society photo inventory and Maine Memory.
A 24-foot steel tower with cab replaced the 1910 wooden tower.
The tower was painted, per the 1916 Forest Commissioner's Report.
Don Hicks began work as a watchman in 1966; his first tower was on Snow Mountain.
A photo caption shows watchman Don Hicks looking out of the tower cab in 1967.
Maine ended its staffed fire-tower system after a budget crisis; after that, some towers were dismantled or collapsed. No source gives a tower-specific date.

notes_for_editor: Build dates (1910 wood, 1914 steel with cab) agree across the Forest Lookouts page and the Maine Memory record. Staffing is documented only for Don Hicks (1966-1967 per the Sun Journal). FFLA and FranklinSites agree the cab is gone; neither gives a date, so no event is dated for the cab loss. Access is the weak point: the summit sits on Penobscot Indian Nation land behind a gate, and no source states a permit or public-visit rule either way, so the access level is set to restricted rather than public. The Maine by Foot and SummitPost pages describe hiking routes, which were used only for the gate and the distance; they do not endorse climbing the structure, and the story says not to. Summit elevation differs across sources (3,948 ft at the tower site per Maine Memory; 3,960 ft and 3,967 ft per FranklinSites and Maine by Foot); not used in the story. Photo candidate Maine Memory record 19137 is not added because its licence was not checked.
